acv.quote: Two hundred and fifty K ACV.

data.reason: Halima, the COO, picked the competitor because it showed the actual people who would answer on an on-sale morning. Jordan points to our better platform, but that is not what decided it.

trigger.action: Lead with what happens when payments fail mid on-sale.
trigger.why: Payments failed four minutes into a big on-sale, and the old provider only replied after it ended.
trigger.quote: payments started failing about four minutes in

decider.action: Tell Halima who answers when things break, not how fast we run.
decider.why: Halima decided alone in one meeting. Ben showed her our load test results and she only said 'good'.
decider.quote: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting

competitor.action: Answer 'who's my person' with real names and on-call people.
competitor.why: Per Ben, the competitor brought its actual account team. Jordan's view that they over-promised is his own unchecked guess.
competitor.quote: someone on call for every major on-sale

message.action: Stop answering 'who's my person' with support tiers and response times.
message.why: Jordan walked Halima through our support plans, and her reply marked the moment the deal was lost.
message.quote: so it's a queue with a faster timer.

proof.action: Add a ticketing customer story about who picked up mid on-sale.
proof.why: Halima wanted to see what we do at minute four. Jordan had ticketing logos but no customer to vouch.
proof.quote: I had logos. I didn't have a person.

words.action: Say 'a name, not a queue' instead of 'support'.
words.why: Nobody at Tixhaven said 'support'. They asked 'who' and talked about 'on-sale morning'.
